incidents.title: Honduran Mother with Brain Surgery History Held Extra Days After Judge Orders Release; Attorney Cannot Find Her
incidents.summary: A Honduran mother of two with a pending asylum case, valid work permit, and recent brain surgery was taken into federal custody. After a judge ordered her release, attorney Danielle Robinson Briand of Justicias Law was repeatedly denied access to her client and could not locate her in the immigration custody system for several days. Upon eventual release, ICE retained the woman's work permit and social security card.

incidents.title: Missing Columbia Heights Fifth Grader Spotted Inside Texas Detention Center by Classmates
incidents.summary: Nearly a month after a Valley View Elementary fifth grader stopped showing up for class with no word from her family, the missing girl was spotted inside the Dilley Immigration Processing Center in Texas. Two of her schoolmates — brothers in second and fifth grade — recognized her after being released from the same facility. At least seven students from Columbia Heights Public Schools have been detained by ICE, ranging in age from five to seventeen.
incidents.location: Valley View Elementary School / Dilley Immigration Processing Center

incidents.title: Two Detained by ICE Inside Hennepin County Courthouse After Hearing
incidents.summary: Federal immigration agents detained two individuals inside the Hennepin County Government Center on February 5 near the security screening area, after a court hearing on criminal sexual conduct charges. Sheriff's deputies aided the detention. Reports indicate a woman was dragged off a Government Center elevator and handed to ICE agents. Chief Public Defender Mike Berger called the arrests unconstitutional, stating detainees were denied access to their attorneys. County Attorney Mary Moriarty said ICE is "degrading public safety by detaining individuals who have not been convicted."

incidents.title: Citing Safety Concerns, Ecuadorian Family Self-Deports Despite Pending Asylum Case
incidents.summary: Carlos Albuja and his family loaded everything they owned into a friend's minivan at 2:45 a.m. on January 30, 2026, and left for Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport with five one-way tickets to Ecuador. The family had pending asylum cases, had no criminal record, and had fled gang violence and extortion in Ecuador. A turning point came when Albuja was blocked by federal agents near the scene of Renee Good's shooting while driving to work. He purchased his own tickets without using the government's CBP Home app. KSTP's 5 INVESTIGATES traveled with the family from Minneapolis to the airport and documented the departure.

incidents.title: Asylum-Seeking Mother Detained at Check-In; Principal Brings Her Children to Whipple
incidents.summary: An asylum-seeking mother of two Valley View Elementary students was detained during an immigration check-in on January 29, 2026. With no family in Minnesota to care for her children (ages 7-9), she asked Principal Jason Kuhlman to bring them to the Whipple Federal Building at Fort Snelling. The eldest child broke into tears upon entering the building.
incidents.latestUpdate: Both children [released from ICE custody and returned to Minnesota](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2026/02/04/minnesota-boys-from-liam-ramos-school-released-from-ice-custody).

incidents.title: Woman Grabbed While Warming Car; Father Detained as "Original Target"
incidents.summary: On the morning of January 29, 2026, ICE agents detained a man in Columbia Heights while his daughter Jessica was warming up her car. An agent grabbed Jessica "very forcefully" and held her wrist and arm for at least five minutes before releasing her when they confirmed she was not their target. Her father, an undocumented immigrant from Ecuador with no criminal record, was taken into custody. Jessica's husband had been detained approximately three weeks earlier, leaving her as the sole caregiver for her daughters.

incidents.title: Food Shelf Volunteer Thao Xiong Detained at Hallie Q. Brown Community Center
incidents.summary: Thao Xiong, a Hmong community activist and food shelf volunteer, was detained by federal agents on January 28, 2026, as he arrived at the Hallie Q. Brown Community Center in St. Paul to help unload a weekly food delivery. Xiong served time in prison and was released in 2016, after which he worked to turn his life around by volunteering and working with local nonprofits. He is the father of a young daughter.
incidents.location: Hallie Q. Brown Community Center, Kent Street

incidents.title: "I Was Yelling at Them to Take Me With Him": Mother Holds Daughter as Husband Detained in Northeast Minneapolis
incidents.summary: ICE agents detained a woman's husband and cousin in a parking lot in Northeast Minneapolis while she held her young daughter in the backseat of their vehicle. Video shows agents pounding on the car window before making the arrests. The woman, identified only as Jenny, pleaded with agents to deport her alongside her husband so the family could stay together, but was left behind with her child. No criminal history has been reported for those detained.

incidents.title: Ecuadorean Man Held 3 Weeks Despite Court Order; Judge Orders ICE Director to Appear for Contempt
incidents.summary: Federal Judge Patrick Schiltz ordered ICE's acting director Todd Lyons to personally appear in court Friday to explain why he should not be held in contempt for violating court orders. The case stems from Juan Hugo Tobay Robles, an Ecuadorean man who entered the United States illegally in 1999 as a minor and has been in custody at Fort Snelling since January 6. Judge Schiltz ordered on January 14 that ICE allow Tobay Robles to challenge his detention at a hearing within a week or release him, finding ICE was holding him under an improper reading of federal law. ICE failed to comply. The judge, appointed by President George W. Bush, wrote that his "patience is at an end" and that while summoning the ICE director was "an extraordinary step," it was necessary because "the extent of ICE's violation of court orders is likewise extraordinary."
incidents.latestUpdate: After his release in Texas, a supporter [drove from Minnesota to Texas](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/01/28/ice-immigrant-minnesota-contempt-released.html) to bring Tobay Robles home to reunite with his family and reestablish his interrupted medical care.

incidents.title: Four Restaurant Workers Detained at El Potro in Brainerd
incidents.summary: Four employees were detained by Homeland Security Investigation agents at El Potro Mexican Restaurant in downtown Brainerd. The Crow Wing County Sheriff's Office assisted with executing two federal felony warrants, but authorities have not explained why four people were taken into custody when only two had warrants. The restaurant closed indefinitely after the operation.
incidents.latestUpdate: [KAXE reports](https://www.kaxe.org/local-news/2026-01-30/ice-arrests-brainerd-restaurant-court-appearances) two of the four detained have been arraigned: **Francisco Javier Montoya-Barboza**, 35, charged with improper entry (misdemeanor), pleaded not guilty; **Jose Barajas-Farias**, 52, charged with reentry of removed alien (felony), pleaded not guilty. Both held at Douglas County Jail in Superior, Wisconsin.
incidents.location: El Potro Mexican Restaurant, South Seventh Street

incidents.title: Lakeville Business Owner Deported to Mexico Despite Two Court Orders
incidents.summary: Emilio Pena Jimenez, a tile installation business owner who has lived in the U.S. since 2000 with no criminal record, was arrested without a warrant at a Walmart in Apple Valley on January 24. Despite two federal court orders — a January 30 temporary restraining order and a February 2 order demanding his immediate release in Minnesota — ICE transported him to the El Paso-Juarez border and released him into Mexico. His attorney alleges he was denied diabetes medication and attorney access in detention, and signed voluntary departure documents under duress.

incidents.title: Church Food Distribution Volunteer Detained at Routine Immigration Check-In
incidents.summary: Alexander William Tique-Marin, a 36-year-old Colombian asylum seeker, was detained on January 23 during a routine immigration check-in appointment related to his ongoing asylum case. Within hours, he was transferred out of Minnesota to Camp East Montana in Texas. Tique-Marin and his family had been dedicated volunteers at La Vina Comunidad Cristiana, a Spanish-speaking church in Burnsville, where they helped distribute food to thousands of families every Monday. He held a full-time job and had complied with every requirement of his immigration case. DHS stated he entered illegally in 2023, was removed, then re-entered in July 2024 and was released by the Biden administration.

incidents.title: 2-Year-Old and Father Detained Near Powderhorn; Flown to Texas Despite Court Order
incidents.summary: ICE agents followed Elvis Joel Tipan Echeverria and his 2-year-old daughter Chloe Renata Tipan Villacis from a grocery store to their home near Chicago Avenue and 35th Street in South Minneapolis, where they detained them. Attorneys for the family say they were asylum-seekers pulled over without a warrant and did not have a final order for removal. A federal judge ordered the toddler released by 9:30 PM, but ICE placed both on a commercial flight to Texas 19 minutes after the order was signed. A government attorney subsequently pledged to return the girl to Minnesota.
incidents.latestUpdate: [ICE flew the 2-year-old and her father to Texas](https://kstp.com/kstp-news/top-news/ice-flew-2-year-old-to-texas-despite-court-order-to-release-her-from-custody/), separating the child from her mother, 19 minutes after a federal judge ordered the toddler released. A government attorney pledged to return the girl to Minnesota on Friday.
incidents.location: Chicago Avenue and 35th Street, South Minneapolis

incidents.title: Four Torture Survivors with Pending Asylum Cases Detained by ICE
incidents.summary: The Center for Victims of Torture, a St. Paul nonprofit, reported that four of their clients - all torture survivors with pending asylum cases, valid work permits, and no criminal records - were detained by ICE. One was reportedly tackled in the snow in front of coworkers while agents laughed. The center warned of severe mental health impacts on their clients due to ICE enforcement.

incidents.title: Hopkins Family of Four Detained; Returned After ICE Violates Court Order
incidents.summary: ICE detained Maria Velasco Hurtado while she was driving to work, then went to the family's Hopkins home and used her detention as leverage to get her husband Luis Fernando Chulca Chiluisa and their two children (ages 7 and 12) to come outside, where they were also detained. Despite a federal court order requiring the family to remain in Minnesota, ICE transported them to Texas. The family's attorney filed a motion for contempt, and the family was returned to Minnesota and released around 1 a.m. on January 27.
incidents.latestUpdate: [Family returned to Minnesota](https://www.hometownsource.com/sun_sailor/free/hopkins-family-detained-by-ice-returned-to-minnesota/article_4a7edf99-2df9-43cd-bc36-afdbf2c991ae.html) around 1 a.m. after ICE complied with court deadline.

incidents.title: Five-Year-Old Liam Ramos Detained in Driveway, Allegedly Used as "Bait"
incidents.summary: Liam Conejo Ramos, a 5-year-old kindergartner, was detained by ICE with his father in their family driveway after arriving home from school on January 20, 2026. School officials allege agents used the child as "bait"—instructing him to knock on the front door to see if anyone else was home. Superintendent Zena Stenvik held an emotional press conference asking, "Why detain a 5-year-old? You can't tell me that this child is going to be classified as a violent criminal." Liam and his father were flown to the Dilley detention center in Texas, where they spent 12 days before a federal judge ordered their release.
incidents.latestUpdate: Next court date set for [February 13](https://bringmethenews.com/minnesota-news/list-of-ice-raids-major-updates-in-minnesota-on-monday-feb-9); family could face deportation by end of that week. DHS [denies seeking quick end](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/02/09/nation/minnesota-immigration-liam-conejo-ramos/) to asylum claims.

incidents.title: Moldovan Refugee Nadya Detained While Driving to Church with Family (NO NEWS MEDIA)
incidents.summary: Nadya, a Moldovan refugee with legal status awaiting her green card, was detained by ICE on January 17, 2026 while driving from her home to church with her husband and three children. Five ICE vehicles stopped the family shortly after they left their house. Despite the family explaining they had refugee status and were in the process of obtaining green cards, ICE detained only Nadya and released her husband and children. She has been held in poor conditions, in handcuffs and sleeping on the floor. **Note: This story seems to follow a pattern of Operation PARRIS (Post-Admission Refugee Reverification and Integrity Strengthening) -- see more details on this below.**

incidents.title: Man Detained While Driving Sick Wife to Emergency Room
incidents.summary: Liborio Parral Ortiz was detained by ICE agents while driving his wife Bonfilia Sanchez Dominguez to the emergency room for severe back pain. Agents blocked their vehicle before they could reach Mercy Hospital Unity Campus in Fridley. Parral Ortiz was taken into custody and transported to El Paso, Texas within 20 hours—before his family could bring him his diabetes medication. His wife was taken to the hospital by ICE agents, but family members and her attorney were blocked from accessing her bedside.

incidents.title: Venezuelan Family Detained, Including 12-Year-Old Sent to Texas
incidents.summary: Federal agents used a battering ram to enter a home on Nevada Avenue East in St. Paul, detaining six residents including a 12-year-old boy. The family immigrated from Venezuela in 2023, and the detained adults possessed work permits and state-issued IDs. The 12-year-old was flown to an immigration detention facility in San Antonio, Texas. Agents claimed to have a search warrant but never displayed one; a warrant that appeared on the doorstep the next day had no case number or file stamp and no record of being filed with the court.
incidents.latestUpdate: Federal judge orders all six family members released after DHS failed to produce warrant by deadline; must be returned to Minnesota within 72 hours.

incidents.title: Two-Year-Old Left Without Parents After ICE Detains Both; DOPA Form Prevents Foster Care
incidents.summary: A two-year-old girl named Scarlett was left without either parent after ICE detained her father approximately three weeks before January 16, 2026, and her mother approximately four days before that date. The child was not taken into government custody only because her parents had previously signed a Delegation of Parental Authority (DOPA) form naming a family friend, Jissica, as her legal guardian. Jissica described Scarlett as "scared of everybody" except her, and said her worst fear was that the child would end up in the foster care system.

incidents.title: NewsGuild Union Member Detained and Transferred to Texas
incidents.summary: A member of the Minnesota Newspaper and Communications Guild was detained by ICE as part of Operation Metro Surge. The individual was transferred to an ICE detention facility in El Paso, Texas, where they are awaiting action on a petition for habeas corpus.

incidents.title: ICE Agents Dine at El Tapatio, Then Return to Detain Workers
incidents.summary: Four ICE agents ate lunch at El Tapatio, a family-owned Mexican restaurant in Willmar, Minnesota around 3 p.m. on January 15. Staff were visibly frightened during the meal. That evening around 8:30 p.m., agents followed the workers after closing and detained three people—the restaurant's owners and a dishwasher—near a Lutheran church and Willmar Middle School. Bystanders blew whistles and confronted the agents during the arrests.
incidents.location: El Tapatio Restaurant, First Street South

incidents.title: Mother Arrested Near Mercado Central; Two Children Left Behind
incidents.summary: A mother was arrested by ICE while cashing a check near Mercado Central on Lake Street. Her two sons, approximately middle-school and high-school age, were left behind at the market where she had dropped them off to get haircuts. Advocates struggled to locate the mother in federal detention because the children did not know her birth date.

incidents.title: Attorneys Denied Access to Detained Clients at Whipple Building
incidents.summary: Multiple attorneys allege the Department of Homeland Security is denying detainees their constitutional right to legal counsel at the Whipple Federal Building in Minneapolis. Four attorneys report being denied access to their clients, including one U.S. citizen and Iraq War veteran detained as a bystander. ICE agents cite reasons attorneys say have no legal basis, including "we don't do attorney visitation."

incidents.title: Two Subcontractors Detained at VINE Faith in Action Senior Center
incidents.summary: Two construction subcontractors were detained by ICE agents while working on exterior repairs at VINE Faith in Action, a senior services facility in Mankato. One worker was apprehended while working on second-floor exterior repairs; the second was detained on the opposite side of the building. The incident occurred in front of elderly members and staff.

incidents.title: Food Shelf Volunteer Detained at Basic Needs in Cottage Grove
incidents.summary: A middle-aged Latino pastor who volunteered at Basic Needs Food Market in Cottage Grove was detained by ICE agents on January 15, 2026. The man had been volunteering several times a week since October, providing translation services for Spanish-speaking customers. ICE agents surveilled the food pantry for two days before making the arrest in the parking lot.
incidents.location: Basic Needs Food Market, 8475 E. Point Douglas Road

incidents.title: Restaurant Worker with Legal Visa Detained by Plain-Clothed Agents
incidents.summary: A restaurant worker at Pancho's Taqueria and Mexican Cafe in Circle Pines with a valid legal work visa was detained by two plain-clothed federal agents lying in wait outside the business around 5 p.m. Surveillance video shows the worker shouting "Ayuda!" (Help!) as agents pulled him from a storage area. The worker, known as Kevin, has no criminal record and fled to the U.S. under asylum protections after a cartel took over his family's factory in his home country. He was transported to the Whipple Federal Building and then to El Paso, Texas within 12 hours. A GoFundMe raised nearly $25,000 for legal fees and family support.
incidents.location: Pancho's Taqueria and Mexican Cafe, Circle Pines

incidents.title: St. Paul Snowplow Driver with Legal Work Status Detained by ICE
incidents.summary: A St. Paul Public Works employee working as a snowplow driver was detained by ICE agents outside a work site despite having valid federal work authorization and a commercial driver's license. Public Works Director Sean Kershaw stated the detention "never should have happened" and that the worker was targeted "purely based on his country of origin." The man is currently being held at a detention facility in El Paso, Texas.

incidents.title: Victor Manuel Díaz Dies in ICE Custody at Camp East Montana After Coon Rapids Arrest
incidents.summary: Victor Manuel Díaz, a 36-year-old Nicaraguan man living in Coon Rapids, died on January 14 at Camp East Montana in El Paso, Texas — eight days after ICE detained him at his workplace. ICE classified his death as a "presumed suicide," but his family and attorney dispute that conclusion. His autopsy was routed to a military hospital rather than the county medical examiner who had ruled the previous detainee death at the same facility a homicide. Díaz is the second of three Minnesotans to die since Operation Metro Surge began.
incidents.location: Camp East Montana, Fort Bliss, El Paso, Texas

incidents.title: Man and Wife Arrested by 12 ICE Agents in Willmar Goodwill Parking Lot; 15-Year-Old Threatened for Filming
incidents.summary: Twelve ICE agents in six vehicles arrested a man and his wife in the Goodwill parking lot in Willmar. Agents did not confirm the man's identity, did not allow him to show documentation, and did not allow him to speak with the Spanish-speaking ICE agent on scene. Fifteen-year-old Adyssey Barrett recorded the arrest on her phone and asked agents to produce a judicial warrant; agents threatened to arrest her. The wife was also handcuffed despite agents yelling confused questions about who she was.

incidents.title: Customer Arrested While Buying Drink at St. Peter Grocery Store
incidents.summary: ICE agents arrested a customer at La Mexicana Market and Restaurant in St. Peter moments after he biked to the store and while he was paying for a drink. When asked for a warrant, agents said they didn't need one in a public area. Business reported significant drop in customers due to fear.
incidents.location: La Mexicana Market and Restaurant, downtown St. Peter

incidents.title: High School Student with Legal Status Arrested in Downtown Willmar
incidents.summary: Suban Noor, a 19-year-old Somali woman and 11th-grade student at Willmar Senior High School, was arrested by ICE agents in downtown Willmar while picking up food for her family. She had legal refugee status (Form I-94) and her family had an active Green Card application. The arrest caused approximately 90% of Somali students to miss school the following day. Noor was released five days later on Friday, Jan 17. **Note: This story seems to follow a pattern of Operation PARRIS (Post-Admission Refugee Reverification and Integrity Strengthening) -- see more details on this below.**

incidents.title: ICE Using El Burrito Mercado as "Hunting Ground" - 47-Year-Old Business Under Siege
incidents.summary: Federal immigration agents have been circling El Burrito Mercado, a prominent 47-year-old Mexican supermarket and restaurant in St. Paul's West Side, for over a week. CEO Milissa Silva-Diaz stated "ICE is using my business as a hunting ground" as unmarked vans and masked agents have scared off customers and workers, forcing the business to close or limit hours. The business has implemented safety measures including posting guards at entrances.
incidents.location: El Burrito Mercado, Cesar Chavez and State Streets, District del Sol

incidents.title: ICE Detains Single Employee at Shearer's Foods Factory in Perham; Agent Claims No Warrant Needed
incidents.summary: ICE agents detained a single employee at Shearer's Foods manufacturing facility in Perham. A witness reported that an ICE agent acknowledged having no warrant and claimed they didn't need one. The agents' vehicles were unmarked and officers were not wearing badges.

incidents.title: Silva Sosa Parents Detained Days After I-130 Approval
incidents.summary: A couple who have lived in Minnesota since 1999 were detained by ICE during a traffic stop in Inver Grove Heights while on their way to work. Five days before the detention, they had received approval on their I-130 petition after working with an immigration lawyer for three years. Their three daughters - Kelsy, Cecilia, and Kimberly Silva Sosa - are now fighting to get their parents released from an El Paso, Texas ICE detention facility. The father is diabetic and the family is uncertain if he is receiving his medication. **Note: This story seems to follow a pattern of Operation PARRIS (Post-Admission Refugee Reverification and Integrity Strengthening) -- see more details on this below.**

incidents.title: North High School Senior Detained at Construction Job, Deported to Ecuador
incidents.summary: Jairo Pitalasig, an 18-year-old senior at North High School in Minneapolis, was detained by ICE at his construction job on January 12. He had been working full-time to support his Ecuadorian family while they sought asylum. His father — who was in remission from cancer — had been detained the day before and sent to El Paso. Both were transferred to Texas. Jairo had missed one routine immigration court date, resulting in an in-absentia removal order. He ultimately accepted deportation to Ecuador.

incidents.title: 50+ ICE Agents Swarm Somali Mall in St. Cloud; Chemical Irritants Used on Protesters
incidents.summary: More than 50 ICE agents descended on Star City Mall, a strip mall with numerous Somali-owned businesses, to arrest one man leaving a deli. Hundreds of protesters gathered and blocked ICE vehicles, leading to a tense standoff. Agents deployed chemical irritants on the crowd. At least four people were detained: the ICE target and three U.S. citizen observers/bystanders who were held for 8-9+ hours at the Whipple Federal Building before being released without charges. The incident came two days after Somali business owners at the same location successfully shouted ICE agents into leaving.

incidents.title: Honduran Man Arrested at Detroit Lakes Restaurant; Partner Documents on Video
incidents.summary: ICE agents arrested a Honduran man outside the China Buffet restaurant in Detroit Lakes. His partner, Grace Waawaate-Ikwe Roberts (a White Earth woman), documented the arrest on video. The detained man was taken to the ICE Field Office at Fort Snelling.

incidents.title: Liberian Man Arrested With Battering Ram, No Judicial Warrant
incidents.summary: Garrison Gibson, a 38-year-old Liberian citizen who has lived in the U.S. for 17 years, was arrested by ICE agents who used a battering ram to enter his north Minneapolis home. His family demanded to see a judicial warrant, but agents presented only an administrative warrant signed by an immigration officer. A 9-year-old child was inside the home during the raid. A federal judge ruled the arrest violated Gibson's Fourth Amendment rights and ordered his immediate release, finding he has "no criminal record" — contradicting DHS claims. Gibson was released but taken back into ICE custody the next day. At a Jan 18 press conference, Gibson alleged agents took "trophy photos" of him and held him in an overcrowded cell. He now wears an ankle monitor and says he is afraid to leave his home.
incidents.latestUpdate: [Full press conference video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UVYy57H30DU) now available from MPR News.

incidents.title: Libyan Man Seeking Medical Treatment Detained, Shackled Despite Skin Condition
incidents.summary: Hani Duglof, 32, who came to Minnesota from Libya in 2014 for life-saving medical treatment for a rare skin condition, was detained by ICE and shackled - despite having a condition that makes his skin as fragile as paper. He has been in the U.S. legally awaiting asylum decision for nearly a decade.
incidents.latestUpdate: [Star Tribune reports](https://www.startribune.com/ice-detainee-with-severe-skin-disorder-going-home/601564192) Duglof was released on bond and returned home to Woodbury.

incidents.title: Soccer Academy Player's Mother Detained at Minneapolis Hotel During Tournament
incidents.summary: The mother of a Forward Madison FC Academy player was detained by immigration authorities at their hotel in Minneapolis while the team was in the Twin Cities for weekend league matches. After the U19 match, the player and his mother went out for lunch and found immigration authorities at their hotel when they returned. The mother was arrested and transferred to custody in Texas, leaving the 18-year-old high school senior from Milwaukee to fend for himself. The exact date of detention is approximate (weekend of Jan 10-11, 2026).

incidents.title: ICE Conducts Door-to-Door Operations in Pelican Rapids
incidents.summary: ICE agents conducted door-to-door operations throughout Pelican Rapids, arresting at least one person: a 43-year-old Nicaraguan man who had lived in the community for three years. The operation caused significant community disruption, with 30 students staying home from school the next day and a local Catholic church canceling its Hispanic Mass. A peaceful protest drew 75-100 participants the following day.

incidents.title: Contractor Detained at General Mills Chanhassen Facility
incidents.summary: ICE agents detained a contractor in the parking lot behind General Mills' Chanhassen manufacturing facility during the second week of January 2026. A 27-second video circulated on social media showing federal immigration officers placing a worker into a gray pickup truck. General Mills confirmed they followed safety protocols and requested agent identification.
incidents.location: General Mills manufacturing facility parking lot

incidents.title: ICE Agents "Ripping People From Cars" at Bus Stop; Union Marks Site as "Abduction" Location
incidents.summary: On January 10, 2026, ICE agents created a chaotic scene at a bus stop at 31st Street and Bloomington Avenue South in Minneapolis, blocking traffic, "ripping people from their cars," and using "excessive force" according to a Metro Transit bus operator who witnessed the incident. The scene caused anxiety and fear for transit workers and passengers. The Amalgamated Transit Union later held a rally at the site, posting a sign reading "Minnesotans were abducted here."
incidents.location: Bus stop at 31st Street and Bloomington Avenue South

incidents.title: Man Pinned and Arrested Inside Maple Grove Walmart
incidents.summary: Six ICE agents arrested a man inside a Walmart in Maple Grove on Saturday night. Video shows agents pinning the individual to the ground inside the store before handcuffing him, escorting him out, and placing him in a red SUV.

incidents.title: DoorDash Driver Arrested by ICE; Wife Flees Into Customer's Home
incidents.summary: Brandon Steven Saenz was arrested by ICE agents when he and his wife arrived at a DoorDash delivery stop in Saint Paul. His wife fled into the customer's home seeking shelter, sparking a tense standoff that was captured on video. The homeowner, a Native American woman, demanded ICE produce a warrant before allowing entry. Police threatened to charge the homeowner with harboring. After a prolonged confrontation, the wife eventually exited and was not detained. The couple's child was in their vehicle during the incident. The wife has since obtained an immigration lawyer and is safe.

incidents.title: Hopkins Father Detained Going to Work; Later Released by Court Order
incidents.summary: Bryam Escobar Martinez, a father of two from Hopkins, was detained by ICE while on his way to work. His wife Estefany Escobar spoke publicly about the family's disruption. Martinez successfully challenged his detention in court and was ordered released within days, becoming one of dozens of detainees to win release through legal challenges.

incidents.title: Immigrant Hospitalized With Skull Fractures After ICE Arrest; Says Beating Was Unprovoked
incidents.summary: Alberto Castañeda Mondragón, a Mexican national who entered the U.S. on a temporary work visa in March 2022 and later overstayed, was detained in St. Paul on January 8, 2026 during Operation Metro Surge. He sustained eight skull fractures and five life-threatening brain hemorrhages while in ICE custody. In his first interview, Castañeda Mondragón told AP that agents pulled him from a friend's car, threw him to the ground, handcuffed him, then punched him and struck his head with a telescoping steel baton (ASP). He says the beating continued at the Ft. Snelling detention facility, where officers "laughed at me and hit me again." ICE officers told hospital staff he "purposefully ran headfirst into a brick wall." A CT scan showed fractures to the front, back, and both sides of his skull — injuries doctors told AP were inconsistent with a fall. A federal judge ruled his arrest was unlawful and ordered his release. He was discharged from HCMC on January 27 with significant memory loss, balance problems, and inability to work.
incidents.latestUpdate: [AP investigation](https://abcnews.go.com/US/wireStory/immigrant-skull-broken-places-ice-arrest-beating-unprovoked-129942949): Castañeda Mondragón recounts being beaten with a telescoping baton during arrest and again at Ft. Snelling. ICE court filing reveals he overstayed his visa. Minnesota leaders call for investigation.
incidents.location: St. Paul (arrest), Whipple Federal Building (processing), HCMC (hospitalized)

incidents.title: Multiple ICE Arrests in Rochester; Activist Documents Agent Using Hammer on Car Window
incidents.summary: ICE conducted enforcement operations across Rochester on January 8-9, 2026, with at least 5 confirmed arrests (27 total arrests in Rochester according to DHS). Activists witnessed concerning tactics including an agent using a hammer to try to open a car window during a warrantless detention. Mayor Kim Norton said the city did not ask for or want ICE presence.
incidents.location: Gates of Rochester complex and various locations

incidents.title: Daycare Teacher with Work Permit Detained Outside Minneapolis Preschool
incidents.summary: A teacher at Jardin Spanish Immersion Academy was detained by ICE agents in tactical gear as she arrived for work on January 7, 2026. Agents removed her from her car directly outside the Minneapolis daycare. According to a GoFundMe page set up by parents, the teacher had a valid work permit through 2030. Her current whereabouts remain unconfirmed, and she had not been released as of January 16.

incidents.title: Teenager Tackled in Snow by ICE Agent
incidents.summary: Video footage verified by the Associated Press shows an ICE agent chasing and tackling a teenager in the snow in Minneapolis on January 7, 2026. The teen, who had been in a car that hit a tree before the foot chase, can be heard yelling "Yo soy legal" ("I am legal" in Spanish) while being restrained face-down in the snow. Minnesota Secretary of State Steve Simon shared the video, calling it "a cruel disgrace." The teenager's identity, legal status, and outcome remain unverified.

incidents.title: Daycare Teacher Tricked with Fake Car Accident Claim, Detained for 10 Minutes
incidents.summary: A teacher at Un Mundo Nuevo Children's Academy was detained by ICE on January 7, 2026, after being lured outside with a false claim that someone had hit her car. When she went outside to check, ICE agents detained her. The daycare told parents she is "a legal resident of this country." She was released approximately 10 minutes later.

incidents.title: Ten-Year-Old Elizabeth Caisaguano Detained with Mother, Held Nearly One Month in Texas
incidents.summary: Elizabeth Zuna Caisaguano, a 10-year-old fourth grader at Highland Elementary in Columbia Heights, was detained by ICE agents with her mother on January 6, 2026, while on their way to school. During the arrest, Elizabeth called her father to say agents would drop her at school—but neither she nor her mother arrived. By day's end, both had been flown to the Dilley Immigration Processing Center in Texas. Elizabeth spent nearly one month in detention before being released on February 3, making her the first and longest-detained of the Columbia Heights students taken during the Trump administration's immigration crackdown.
incidents.latestUpdate: Elizabeth and her mother [released from Dilley](https://sahanjournal.com/education/columbia-heights-fourth-grader-held-by-ice/) Tuesday evening after nearly one month in detention. They were at a Texas shelter Wednesday morning before returning to Minnesota to reunite with her father.
incidents.location: On way to Highland Elementary School

incidents.title: Chilean Man Agrees to Voluntary Departure, Offers to Pay Own Airfare — Still Stuck in Louisiana Jail Five Weeks Later
incidents.summary: Gonzalo Torres, a Chilean national living in Burnsville, was arrested by ICE on January 6. He signed a voluntary departure agreement on January 8 and asked to buy his own plane ticket home, but was refused. Five weeks and three cancelled government flights later, he remains detained at Richwood Correctional Center in Louisiana, where he has described bathrooms overflowing with excrement and eating off the floor.

incidents.title: Man Seeks Refuge in Bloomington Office During 6-Hour ICE Standoff
incidents.summary: Aldrin Maldonado, a man being pursued by ICE agents, fled on foot and took refuge inside the Wilderness Inquiry office building in Bloomington. Pleading with office workers — "It's ICE. I have family here, please" — he was allowed to remain in the vestibule while staff denied ICE entry, citing lack of a judicial warrant. After a six-hour standoff with negotiations through an interpreter, Maldonado voluntarily surrendered after ICE presented a felony arrest warrant. He was taken to the Whipple Building and later transferred to Texas. His girlfriend later said: "It's hard when the kids ask where he is."

incidents.title: Restaurant Owner Reported Missing, Confirmed Detained by ICE
incidents.summary: Juan Manuel Arellano Zepeda, 48, owner of El Fresco restaurant in Bloomington, was detained by ICE after leaving his Apple Valley home for work. His family initially reported him missing after ICE declined to confirm his detention. They only confirmed he was in custody after seeing him in a DHS social media video.
incidents.location: Apple Valley / El Fresco Restaurant, Bloomington

incidents.title: Indigenous Ecuadorian Mother Detained, Leaving 10 Children Including 5-Month-Old Infant
incidents.summary: Melida Rita Wampash Tuntuam, a 41-year-old Indigenous Ecuadorian mother who worked as an office cleaner, was detained by ICE in early January. She left behind 10 children, including a 5-month-old infant who is a U.S. citizen. Her 20-year-old son quit his restaurant job to care for his siblings. ICE agents surrounded the family's home twice seeking additional family members. Community volunteers have been sheltering the children at a safe house in south Minneapolis.

incidents.title: ICE Raids TruNorth Solar Factory in Arden Hills - "First Big One of 2026"
incidents.summary: ICE agents raided TruNorth Solar factory in Arden Hills, Minnesota on January 2, 2026, described as "the first big one of 2026." Protesters gathered outside the facility blowing whistles, honking horns, and yelling at agents to leave.

incidents.title: Patient Shackled to Hospital Bed by ICE for 28 Hours Without Warrant
incidents.summary: ICE agents entered Hennepin County Medical Center's emergency department without a judicial warrant and remained at a patient's bedside for approximately 28 hours. The patient was handcuffed and shackled to their bed despite medical staff objections. Agents were eventually removed after county commissioners and hospital leadership intervened.

incidents.title: ICE Agent Fires Shots at Man During St. Paul Arrest After Being Struck by Vehicle
incidents.summary: An ICE agent fired two shots at Juan Carlos Romero, a Cuban national, during an arrest attempt in St. Paul on December 21, 2025, after Romero struck two agents with his SUV. No one was hit by gunfire. Two ICE officers were hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries. Romero, who entered the U.S. in 2024 through the Biden administration's CBP One app, allegedly refused to comply with a vehicle stop, struck one agent while driving away, rammed an ICE vehicle at his apartment complex striking a second agent, then attempted to flee on foot. During his apprehension, he bit an ICE agent. ICE blamed "sanctuary politicians" for creating conditions that led to the confrontation.

incidents.title: Construction Workers Take Refuge on Roof During Hours-Long ICE Standoff
incidents.summary: Two construction workers and brothers, Edgar and Marco Chicaiza Dutan, took refuge on an unfinished roof frame at a townhome construction site in the Avienda development in Chanhassen as approximately 10-15 ICE agents surrounded them. The standoff lasted roughly four hours in temperatures of negative four degrees with steady winds of 10-20 mph. Agents denied community members' requests to provide hand warmers or blankets to the men on the roof. As the crowd grew to approximately 100 people — many of whom had completed local bystander training — and news crews arrived, ICE eventually departed. Edgar came down first and was hospitalized at Ridgeview Hospital before being transferred to ICE custody at Freeborn County Adult Detention Center. Marco remained in the rafters until after agents left. Both were hospitalized in satisfactory condition. State Rep. Alex Falconer reported that agents lacked a judicial warrant and "didn't know who they were trying to find." The Carver County Sheriff's Office had not been given prior notice of the operation.
incidents.latestUpdate: Major enrichment from CBS News, Carver County Local News, EP Local News. Added full timeline, witness accounts, official statements, community response details, DHS statements. Added 5 new sources. Upgraded trustworthiness to HIGH.

incidents.title: Brooklyn Park Cook Arrested Outside Workplace; Restaurant Forced to Close
incidents.summary: Jorge Vergara Rubio, an Ecuadorian cook, was arrested by ICE outside his employer Crumbs and Coffee in Brooklyn Park. His employer claims Rubio was legally authorized to work at the time of arrest, though ICE states his employment authorization application was denied in September 2025. The restaurant was forced to close following the arrest.

incidents.title: 13-Year-Old Boy Handcuffed, Thrown to Ground by ICE Agents
incidents.summary: ICE agents detained Gomez outside an Eden Prairie apartment complex while his 13-year-old son Jose was handcuffed, allegedly thrown to the ground, and struck by officers. Jose was later released but experienced medical complications including abnormal heartbeat that required hospitalization at St. Francis Hospital.

incidents.title: Parents Separated from 7-Year-Old in Burnsville Raid; Ring Camera Captures Forced Entry
incidents.summary: ICE agents raided a home on McAndrews Road in Burnsville, breaking down doors and detaining four people including both parents of a 7-year-old child. Ring camera footage captured agents following a couple home from grocery shopping and the subsequent forced entry. U.S. citizens in the home reported guns pointed at them. One detained father had a valid work permit.

incidents.title: ICE Agents Point Weapons at Students During Campus Arrest at Augsburg University
incidents.summary: ICE agents detained undergraduate student Jesus Saucedo-Portillo in Parking Lot B at Augsburg University, a private campus in Minneapolis. University officials said agents pointed weapons at students and staff, including those watching from residence hall windows, and refused to produce a judicial warrant when asked. DHS disputed this account, claiming agents had a warrant and were obstructed by a university administrator.

incidents.title: Church Employee Deported, Parish Later Surveilled by ICE
incidents.summary: Francisco Paredes, a 46-year-old church maintenance worker and choir member who had lived in the U.S. for 25 years, was arrested by ICE in the parking lot of St. Gabriel the Archangel Catholic Church in Hopkins. He spent a month in detention, including Christmas without religious services, before being deported to Mexico. On January 4, 2026, ICE agents were observed surveilling the church during Spanish Mass.
incidents.location: St. Gabriel the Archangel Catholic Church, 13th Avenue South

incidents.title: Addiction Recovery Leader Detained, Labeled "Gang Member" — Later Released by Federal Judge
incidents.summary: Abdulkadir Sharif Abdi, 47, a Somali refugee and well-known addiction recovery counselor, was detained by ICE on December 1, 2025, at his Minneapolis home. Federal officials alleged he was a current gang member and said they had "orders" and a warrant for his arrest. ICE labeled him among the "worst of the worst" on the DHS website. However, Abdi's last conviction was over a decade ago, and in 2018 a federal judge noted he had "worked to turn his life around" since 2007. Just before Christmas, government attorneys withdrew their opposition to his release. A federal judge in Nebraska barred ICE from detaining him again. Despite his release, Abdi remains featured on the DHS "worst of the worst" website. A Star Tribune investigation of the 240 names DHS released found that while 80% had felony convictions, nearly all had already served their time and were not actively wanted by police.

incidents.title: Hola Arepa Staff Refuses ICE Entry Without Warrant
incidents.summary: Two plain-clothed ICE agents entered Hola Arepa restaurant during dinner service, claiming to search for someone. When general manager Naomi Rathke demanded to see a judicial warrant, the agents said "We don't need a warrant." Rathke refused entry to the kitchen and the agents eventually left without detaining anyone. The restaurant closed early and safely escorted employees to their cars.

incidents.title: Somali-American Metro Transit Bus Driver Detained Over a Month
incidents.summary: A Somali-American Metro Transit bus operator was detained by ICE on December 2, 2025, while on his way to work. He was held in ICE detention facilities in Iowa and Nebraska for over a month before being released without explanation on January 6, 2026. The Amalgamated Transit Union Local 1005 called the detention "unlawful."

incidents.title: Man With Legal Protection Status Detained at Restaurant; Vehicle Abandoned
incidents.summary: Jose, a Salvadoran immigrant with legal withholding-of-removal protection status (a form of legal protection meant to prevent deportation), was detained by federal agents during lunch at Lomabonita restaurant on St. Paul's East Side. Agents abandoned his vehicle with construction tools on Margaret Street and White Bear Avenue.
incidents.location: Lomabonita restaurant, Margaret Street and White Bear Avenue

incidents.title: House Painter Arrested After 5-Hour Standoff; Family Reports Humiliation, No Warrant Shown
incidents.summary: Jeffrey Suazo, a 26-year-old house painter from Honduras, was arrested after a 5-hour standoff with ICE agents on St. Paul's East Side. Federal agents pursuing a different man (Victor Rodriguez) followed Suazo when he fled upon seeing federal activity. Family members report agents entered without showing a warrant and taunted/humiliated them during the standoff. Over 200 protesters gathered, leading to deployment of pepper spray and nonlethal munitions.

incidents.title: 14 Workers Detained in Major ICE Workplace Raid at Bro-Tex
incidents.summary: Federal agents raided Bro-Tex Inc., a cleaning products manufacturer in St. Paul, detaining 14 workers in what organizers called the largest ICE workplace raid in Minnesota in 2025. Protesters who attempted to block agents' vehicles were pepper sprayed. Gov. Walz said the state received "no heads up" from federal authorities.
incidents.location: Bro-Tex Inc., 830 N. Hampden Ave (off University Ave)

incidents.title: Adán Núñez Gonzalez Forcibly Arrested in Northfield, Son Records
incidents.summary: Adán Núñez Gonzalez, a Northfield house painter and father of four who had lived in the community for over a decade, was forcibly arrested by ICE agents who boxed in his vehicle with four unmarked SUVs, broke his car window, and extracted him at gunpoint without showing a warrant. His 15-year-old son witnessed the arrest and recorded video, heard saying "Hey, put the gun down, that's my dad." One agent was photographed wearing a patch reading "deplorable" — an ICE spokesperson called this "deplorable" and said the agency would investigate. Over 200 community members attended a vigil in his support. Núñez Gonzalez was subsequently denied asylum and deported to Mexico.
incidents.latestUpdate: [MPR News reports](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2025/11/24/adan-nunez-gonzalez-northfield-man-arrested-by-ice-to-be-deported-to-mexico) Núñez Gonzalez denied asylum and will be deported to Mexico.
incidents.location: Washington Street & E Ames Street, Northfield
